solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Absolute evil

definitions.meaning: absolute in the sense of utter or outrageous, as in a dreadful, appalling liberty

explanation.walkthrough: The blogger read this as one plain definition, but 'absolute' works on its own too: something utter or outrageous, as in 'a diabolical liberty'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fiendishly wicked and, colloquially, utterly dreadful, matching each clue word in turn.

clue.text: Sharon for example is creating interest with real bust?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of real are smashed and rebuilt

parts.note: i is the standard abbreviation for interest, as in interest rates

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone called Sharon is causing a stir with a real bosom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' turns REAL into RAEL. Sharon is Ariel Sharon, the former Israeli prime minister, not a woman's first name; the question mark warns of the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel Sharon was a prime minister of Israel, so he is one example of a citizen of that country.

clue.text: Labour politician's nonsense

definitions.meaning: Ed ..., the British Labour Party politician and former shadow chancellor
British slang for rubbish or drivel

explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of Britain's two main political parties; Ed Balls was a senior Labour figure when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Ed Balls doubles as the vulgar British slang word for rubbish talk.

clue.text: Almost all beer — it's drunk for free

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger about into a new order
almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nearly all the beer is downed without paying for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims ALL to AL; 'drunk' shuffles AL + BEER + IT. The 's is 'is', a link, and 'for' joins to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone is to set them free, so the verb is a synonym of free.

clue.text: Coloured and showy bird on ground? That's an imaginary situation

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for coloured listed in Chambers
loud clothes are garish and showy
the cuckoo is a familiar bird
land means ground or earth

explanation.surface: A gaudy bird perched on the earth, which turns out to be a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: C for coloured is rare outside Chambers. 'on' just puts the bird before the ground in the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamland of absurdly unrealistic hopes is a fanciful, imaginary state of affairs.

clue.text: Child left a duke to perish

parts.note: to perish means to die

explanation.surface: A youngster abandoned an aristocrat to his death.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for a boy or young lad, so a child.

clue.text: Difficult to ignore son's argument

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: stiff can mean difficult, as in a stiff test
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone's quarrel with their son is hard to overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after son is a link ('has'), not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor quarrel or petty squabble is a mild kind of argument.

clue.text: Boy comfortable raising arms?

parts.note: Tommy is a boy's name

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: snug means comfortable and cosy

explanation.surface: A lad at ease lifting his arms in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns SNUG into GUNS; 'arms' looks like limbs but means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Submachine guns of the Thompson type are firearms, and arms means weapons.

clue.text: Abandon in favour of drink

parts.note: being for something means being in favour of it
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Giving up something for the sake of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To forsake is to desert or give up, the same as abandon.

clue.text: Decaying molar male's pulled out of the mouth

indicators.note: decaying suggests the tooth crumbling, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rotten back tooth being pulled out by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: MOLAR rearranged with M removed ('pulled out') leaves the answer; the tooth hints at the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral is the adjective relating to the mouth, as in oral hygiene.

clue.text: Cruel to spoil end of story — it could be an eye-opener

parts.note: bloody can mean cruel and violent
to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: end of means take the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Telling someone a story's ending is a cruel spoiler.
explanation.walkthrough: An eye-opener is a drink taken in the morning to wake up; this vodka and tomato cocktail is a classic hangover cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A vodka and tomato juice cocktail is often drunk in the morning as a pick-me-up.

clue.text: One lets in uncles sorrowfully

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone admits their uncles into the house with sadness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lets' looks like 'allows' but means rents out.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who leases property to a tenant is someone who lets.

clue.text: I'm a randy, strange fellow who does things with milk?

definitions.text: fellow who does things with milk?

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters take an odd new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lecherous oddball confesses to unusual activities with milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who works in a dairy handles and sells milk.

clue.text: I just realised about leaders in institutions using Japanese art of self-defence

indicators.note: about means around, so one set of letters goes around the other
realised read as made real or formed suggests reworking the letters
leaders in points to the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone suddenly understands institutions teaching a Japanese martial art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'realised' shuffles I JUST into JITSU, and 'about' puts it around IUJ. 'Japanese' feels part of the definition but gives J.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Japanese martial art of unarmed combat used for self-defence.

clue.text: Alternative way to make your wheels turn over?

definitions.text: Alternative way to make your wheels turn over?

parts.words: Alternative way to make your wheels turn over?
parts.note: a car with a flat battery can be started by using leads from another car or by pushing it, the engine turning over

explanation.definitionFit: Starting a car's engine with jump leads or a push is an alternative to the ignition key.

clue.text: Heads of universities seem extremely dubiously employed

indicators.note: heads of means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: University chiefs look very suspiciously like they are in work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used has been put to use, so employed is a synonym.

clue.text: Red clay plastered bottom of gown — you may need to do this to it

definitions.text: you may need to do this to it

indicators.note: plastered means drunk, so the letters stagger into another order
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A gown smeared with red clay at its hem needs special cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the gown; 'plastered' looks like smeared but shuffles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes like a gown are cleaned with chemical solvents rather than water, which is what you would do to it.

clue.text: Check source of power after acceleration's dropped?

indicators.note: dropped means let fall away, so a letter goes

parts.note: steam powered engines and turbines
a is the symbol for acceleration in physics

explanation.surface: Inspecting a power source after a car stops speeding up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check or stop it.

clue.text: Pain in most of aquatic bird's beak

indicators.note: in places one word inside another
most of drops the final letter

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A water bird's bill hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' looks like a bill but is old British school slang for a teacher or headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Beak is British slang for a schoolmaster, so it means a teacher.

clue.text: Oil spread around sore knee

indicators.note: spread around scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Rubbing oil on a painful knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin oil, used as fuel for lamps and heaters, is a kind of oil.

clue.text: African city's rain altered by witchcraft

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: obi is a form of West Indian sorcery

explanation.surface: A city's weather changed by magic.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Kenya is a city in Africa.

clue.text: Assist criminal's arrest

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Helping arrest a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrest' is not a police detention but a halt, a state of standstill.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrest can mean a stopping, and stasis is a state of standstill.

clue.text: Wrong temperature in telegraph office — it sounds high

parts.note: false means wrong
TO is an abbreviation for telegraph office

explanation.surface: An error about heat in a telegraph office, with a high-pitched sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto voice is unnaturally high-pitched, so it sounds high.

clue.text: Food beginning to go off in box

indicators.note: the beginning going off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: scoff is British slang for food
taken as written

explanation.surface: Food starting to rot inside a box.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOFF is British slang for food; 'beginning to go off' drops its S. The blogger could not parse it; a commenter gave this reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffin is the box in which a dead body is buried.

clue.text: One employed by large hospital trust

indicators.note: employed by means taken on inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: fat means large
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone taken on by a big hospital trust.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith and trust are synonyms for belief in someone.

clue.text: Possibly keep cash — a tendency initially one has?

definitions.text: Possibly keep cash — a tendency initially one has?

indicators.note: has means holds, so the outer letters contain the others
possibly suggests one possible arrangement of the letters
initially points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A habit of hanging on to money that someone has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' shuffles KEEP CASH into CHEAPSKE, which 'has' A plus T (first of 'tendency') inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserly person who avoids spending money tends to keep cash.

clue.text: Figure what groom might say touching tail of foal

parts.note: a bridegroom says I do in the wedding vows

indicators.note: tail of means the last letter

explanation.surface: A horse groom talks about the end of a foal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' suggests a stable hand with horses but here is a bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a figure or statue worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Rubbish tip in grave decay

indicators.note: tip means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: rot means decay

explanation.surface: Rubbish dumped at a rubbish tip decomposing in a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a rubbish dump in this surface. GROT is British slang for junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Grot is British slang for rubbish or worthless stuff.

clue.text: A rich eccentric is after car seat

indicators.note: is after places the second piece behind the first

parts.note: a sedan is a saloon car

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wealthy oddball wants a car seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles.
